name: P I Industries Ltd
about: PI Industries Ltd is a leading player in the agro-chemicals space having strong presence in both Domestic and Export markets. It has state-of-art facilities in Gujarat having integrated process development teams with in-house engineering capabilities. [1]

sections.one_liner: Indian agrochemical contract manufacturer and innovator. Earnings fell 39% for two straight quarters; the question is whether exports recover.
business: Makes crop protection products and biologicals, offers pharma contract research and manufacturing (CRDMO), and is entering specialty and electronic chemicals [AR FY26]
Three segments: crop protection & biologicals, pharma CRDMO, specialty & electronic chemicals. Segment revenue shares not disclosed [AR FY26]
Main engine is agrochemical exports made to order (CSM): order book stable at $1.2bn, contract assets Rs750cr [Q1FY27 call]
Domestic agri revenue +3% on 12% volume growth, so prices fell about 9%. Biologicals +50%. Geographic split not disclosed [Q1FY27 call; AR FY26]
financial_snapshot: Q1FY27: revenue Rs1,702cr (-10.4% YoY), EBITDA Rs367cr at 22% margin, PAT Rs244cr (-39.0% YoY) [Numbers]
Last four quarters: revenue Rs6,515cr, EBITDA Rs1,547cr (23.7% margin), PAT Rs1,164cr. Market cap Rs31,690cr is 27x that PAT [Numbers]
Margin has been 22% for three straight quarters, against 27–29% in Jun–Sep 2025 [Numbers]
P/E 29.4, P/B 2.8x, ROCE 15%, ROE 11.2%, dividend yield 0.72%. Price Rs2,089: 4% above 52-week low, 45% below high [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue grew 8.0% a year over 5 years but only 1.1% over 3; FY26 revenue fell 15.8% to Rs6,714cr [Numbers]
PAT grew 12.3% a year over 5 years, 2.4% over 3; FY26 PAT -20.4% to Rs1,321cr, and quarterly declines are widening [Numbers]
Annual margin rose 22% (FY21) to 28% (FY25), then 26% in FY26; the 22% quarterly run-rate means FY27 could fall further [Numbers]
ROCE fell from 24% (FY24) to 15% (FY26). Management says asset turns fell from 2.5x to 1.5x on Rs2,600cr of capex [Numbers; May 2026 call]
balance_sheet: Borrowings rose from Rs46cr (FY23) to Rs342cr (FY26), still minor: debt/equity 0.03 on net worth of Rs11,230cr [Numbers]
Working capital days rose 48→120 from FY24 to FY26; debtor days 44→88, inventory days 124→157, cash cycle 42→119 days [Numbers]
Management cites Rs3,427cr cash, so net cash is about Rs3,085cr (~10% of market cap); Q1 released Rs300cr, cutting working capital 19 days [May 2026 call; Q1FY27 call]
cash_quality: FY26 operating cash flow (CFO) was Rs474cr against PAT of Rs1,321cr, only 0.36x; the 3-year average is 0.84x [Numbers]
Free cash flow fell from Rs1,417cr to Rs575cr to -Rs632cr over FY24–FY26. Implied FY26 capex Rs1,106cr, up from Rs619cr in FY24 [Numbers]
3-year free cash flow totals Rs1,360cr, 29% of Rs4,663cr PAT. Working capital, not capex alone, is absorbing the profits [Numbers]
narrative_vs_numbers: Management keeps citing '3-year CAGR growth', but 3-year revenue CAGR is 1.1% and PAT CAGR 2.4% [May 2026 call; Numbers]
Gross margin held at 57–58% but EBITDA margin fell from 27% to 22%: costs below gross profit are absorbing about 5 points, likely pharma and biologicals [Q1FY27 call; Numbers]
The 'strong cash balance' sits next to -Rs632cr free cash flow and 120 working-capital days. The cash pile is shrinking [May 2026 call; Numbers]
Dec-2025 PAT (Rs311cr) exceeded EBITDA (Rs302cr), implying large other income or one-offs. Not explained in the material [Numbers]
guidance: FY27 revenue growth cut to 'lower single digit' (Aug), from 'late single to early double digit at worst' (May). Q1 came in at -10.4% [Q1FY27 call; Numbers]
FY27 capex raised to Rs700–800cr (May, kept in Aug) from Rs500–600cr (Feb), above FY26 operating cash flow of Rs474cr [Q1FY27 call; Numbers]
Keep FY27 gross margin at FY26's 58%. No EBITDA margin guidance: management calls it 'difficult to guide' [May 2026 call]
Tax rate to rise to about 24% in FY27, from 22% in FY26; in Nov 2025 it had guided 22–23% for 2–3 years [Q1FY27 call; Nov 2025 call]
Pharma EBITDA break-even needs Rs500–600cr revenue within 2+ years; electronic chemicals target about $100m in 4–5 years [May 2026 call]

ledger.promised: Modest recovery in Q4 (Nov 2025 call); sequential improvement and volume growth from Q4 (Feb 2026 call)
ledger.delivered: Revenue Rs1,565cr, +13.7% QoQ but -12.4% YoY; PAT -39.4% YoY

ledger.promised: Hold FY26 EBITDA margin at 25–26% (Feb 2026 call)
ledger.delivered: FY26 margin 25.8% (Rs1,732cr / Rs6,714cr), but Q4 was only 22%

ledger.promised: Tax rate 22–23% for the next 2–3 years (Nov 2025 call)
ledger.delivered: FY26 at 22%, but FY27 raised to ~24% six months later

ledger.promised: Pharma EBITDA positive within one year (Nov 2025 call)
ledger.delivered: Reset to 2+ years at Rs500–600cr revenue (May); analyst cites Rs550cr losses

ledger.promised: Growth late single to early double digit at worst (May 2026 call)
ledger.delivered: Cut to lower single digit in Aug; Q1 revenue -10.4% YoY

ledger.promised: Maintain FY26 gross margin of 58% (May 2026 call)
ledger.delivered: Q1 gross margin 57%; EBITDA margin 22% vs 27% a year ago

ledger.promised: Domestic agrochemical growth 'back on track' from FY27 (Feb 2026 call)
ledger.delivered: Q1 domestic revenue +3%, volume +12%, prices down about 9%

ledger.promised: Capex Rs500–600cr (Feb 2026 call), raised to Rs700–800cr (May 2026 call)
ledger.delivered: Not yet reportable; the range was raised 33% within three months

bull: About Rs3,085cr net cash (~10% of market cap) and debt/equity of 0.03 fund Rs700–800cr capex without stress [May 2026 call; Numbers]
Stable $1.2bn order book; new products are 16–18% of contract-manufacturing revenue; first in-house molecule (Pioxaniliprole) launches in India in FY27 [Q1FY27 call]
Q1 working capital fell 19 days and released Rs300cr; reversing to FY24's 48 days would free far more cash [Q1FY27 call; Numbers]
bear: P/E 29.4 on PAT down 39% two quarters running; ROE 11.2% does not justify 2.8x book [Numbers]
FY27 growth guidance cut within three months; Q1 at -10.4% means the rest of the year must grow just to reach low single digits [Q1FY27 call; Numbers]
Patent risk on the largest contract-manufacturing product (Pyroxasulfone), plus Rs550cr pharma losses, puts the 22% margin at risk of further compression [May 2026 call; Q1FY27 call]
questions: What growth do Q2–Q4 need to hit low single digits after Q1's -10.4%?
Gross margin held at 57%; which cost lines took EBITDA margin from 27% to 22%?
What explains Dec-2025 PAT of Rs311cr exceeding EBITDA of Rs302cr?
How much Pyroxasulfone revenue faces generics, and when does exclusivity end?

analyst_pushback.summary: Saurabh Jain: INR 2,600 crore capex not converting; asset turns fell 2.5x to 1.5x. Management: Multi-year ramp-up takes 4-5 years for new molecule capacities to mature.
Tejas Pradhan: New product absolute revenue flat YoY despite rising % mix. Management: Global agriculture challenging; expect improvement as situation stabilizes.
Tejas Pradhan: INR 700 crore still above FY25 levels. Management: Will maintain this range given business model and supply chain volatility management needs.
Vivek Rajamani: EBITDA fell from 27-28% to 22%. Management: Target is to manage margins but difficult to guide specifically given volatility.

annual_report.business: PI Industries is a life sciences company originating from India. It develops and manufactures crop protection products, biologicals, pharma CRDMO services, and specialty chemicals. It serves global agricultural and pharmaceutical markets through innovation-led solutions.

segments.name: Crop Protection & Biologicals
segments.comment: Core agri-sciences business including insecticides and plant health solutions

segments.name: Pharma CRDMO
segments.comment: Contract research, development and manufacturing services for pharmaceuticals

annual_report.revenue_mix: Global operations: India, US, LATAM, Mexico, UK. Products span crop protection, biologicals, pharma services, specialty chemicals. Specific geographic/product percentages not disclosed.
strategy: Innovation-led growth: originate molecules in India for global markets
Advance proprietary pipeline including new chemical entities (NCE)
Scale pharma CRDMO platform for contract services expansion
Build biologicals platform for sustainable crop protection solutions
Diversify into electronic chemicals and specialty segments
annual_report.outlook: Entering 80th year focused on pioneering innovation in life sciences from India to world. Plans to take new active ingredients to global markets, scale pharma services platform, and expand across sectors creating multiple growth pathways.
risks: Geopolitical realignments and shifting trade dynamics affecting supply chain
Climate variability and changing weather patterns impacting agricultural demand
Increasing regulatory scrutiny on agrochemicals and life sciences products
Supply chain resilience and diversification requirements in volatile markets
